questionText: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct in the context of CPU scheduling?
options: The goal is to only maximize CPU utilization and minimize throughput.
Round-robin policy can be used even when the CPU time required by each of the processes is not known apriori.
Implementing preemptive scheduling needs hardware support.
explanation:
Statement (A) is correct: Turnaround time is defined as $\text{Turnaround Time} = \text{Burst Time} + \text{Waiting Time}$, which directly includes waiting time.

Statement (B) is incorrect: The primary objective of CPU scheduling is to maximize both CPU utilization and throughput (not minimize throughput).

Statement (C) is correct: Round-robin scheduling is a preemptive policy based on time slicing, so it does not require prior knowledge of the CPU burst time of each process.

Statement (D) is correct: Preemptive scheduling requires hardware timer interrupts to periodically transfer control back to the operating system scheduler.

Therefore, statements A, C, and D are correct.
